certificate.title: Set Up the Bank Reconciliation Skill in Claude Cowork Completion

course.description: Build a reusable Cowork task that matches bank transactions to invoices, flags missing or mismatched items, and outputs a clean reconciliation report — ready to run every month in minutes.
learningOutcomes: Apply the methods taught in Set Up the Bank Reconciliation Skill in Claude Cowork.

lessons.content:
The **Bank Reconciliation** skill is a saved Cowork task that acts as your reconciliation assistant. Each time you run it, you provide your bank statement and your books — it matches them, flags gaps, and outputs a formatted recon report.

**What it handles:**
- Matches bank transactions line-by-line to your invoices or ledger entries
- Flags transactions present in the bank but missing from the books (and vice versa)
- Identifies amount mismatches or duplicate entries
- Outputs a clean reconciliation report showing matched, unmatched, and flagged items

**Why build it as a skill:** Once set up, you reuse the same task every month. Just swap in the new data — the instructions stay the same.
lessons.title: What this skill does

lessons.content:
1. Open **Claude Cowork** on your desktop
2. Click **New Task**
3. Name it: **Bank Reconciliation**
4. Leave the task open — the next step is where you write the instructions that make this a real skill

> **Note:** In Cowork, a "skill" is simply a task with good instructions. The name you give it is what you'll see every time you open it. Keep it short and descriptive — "Bank Reconciliation" is perfect.
lessons.title: Create the task in Cowork

activities.title: Write the skill instructions (this is the skill)

lessons.content:
In the task instructions field, paste the prompt below. This defines what Claude does every time you run this skill. **Replace the example details with your actual process — the more specific you are, the better the output.**

---

*"You are my Bank Reconciliation assistant. Each time I run this task, I will upload two files: my bank statement and my general ledger or invoice register for the same period.*

*When I provide the files, do the following:*

*1. Match each bank transaction to a corresponding entry in the ledger by date, amount, and reference number*
   *→ Replace this with your actual matching criteria (e.g. do you match by invoice number? vendor name? both?)*

*2. Flag any bank transactions with no matching ledger entry*
   *→ Replace with your threshold: do you flag everything, or only items over a certain amount?*

*3. Flag any ledger entries with no matching bank transaction*
   *→ Note if there are timing differences you want excluded (e.g. outstanding cheques, deposits in transit)*

*4. Identify duplicate transactions — same amount, date, and payee appearing more than once*

*5. Output a reconciliation report with three sections:*
   *→ Matched items (summary count and total)*
   *→ Unmatched items (detailed list with amounts)*
   *→ Flagged exceptions (duplicates, mismatches)*

*6. End with a one-line reconciliation statement: Opening balance + receipts – payments = closing balance. Confirm it agrees to the bank statement closing balance.*
   *→ Replace with your actual reconciliation format if different*

*Do not finalise the report until all checks pass. If something doesn't balance, tell me what's wrong before showing the output."*

---

> **Make it yours:** Swap in your account names, ERP field names, and any firm-specific rules. The more context you give Claude about your process, the less you'll need to fix in the output.
lessons.title: Write the skill instructions (this is the skill)

activities.title: Run it and save your skill

lessons.content:
Your skill is ready. Here's how to use it the first time and every time after.

**First run:**
1. Open the **Bank Reconciliation** task you just set up
2. Upload your bank statement and ledger/invoice file for the current period
3. Let Claude work through the matching — review the output
4. If anything looks off, refine the instructions in the task and run again
5. Once the output is exactly what you need, you're done setting up

**Every month after that:**
1. Open the **Bank Reconciliation** task
2. Upload the new period's files
3. Review the reconciliation report — matched, unmatched, flagged
4. Export or copy the output into your working papers

**Tips:**
- The task saves automatically — you never need to rewrite the instructions
- If your process changes (new ERP, new matching rules), just edit the task instructions once
- The more consistent your file format, the faster and cleaner the output will be

You now have a reusable Bank Reconciliation skill that runs in minutes instead of hours.
